subject: Wi-Fi not working on a phone
query: why is wifi not working on my phone
title: Why is Wi-Fi not working on my phone? Fixes for iPhone and Android
answer: Most often, Wi-Fi stops working on a phone because of a temporary glitch in the phone or router, Airplane Mode or a VPN getting in the way, a saved network with an old password, or an internet outage. Start by turning Wi-Fi off and on, restarting the phone and router, and testing another device. If only your phone fails, forget the network and rejoin it.
body:
First, find out where the problem is. If other phones and laptops on the same Wi-Fi also can't get online, the problem is the router or your internet provider, not your phone. If your phone connects fine to a different network, such as at work or a friend's house, your home network is the likely cause. If the phone shows it is connected but pages won't load ("No Internet Connection" on iPhone), the Wi-Fi link works but the internet behind it doesn't.

What to try, in order:

1. Toggle Wi-Fi off and on, and make sure Airplane Mode is off.
2. Restart the phone.
3. Restart the router and modem: unplug both, wait about 15 seconds, plug them back in and wait until the lights look normal.
4. Forget the network and rejoin it with the current password. On Android (Pixel): Settings > Network & internet > Internet > Saved networks > tap the network > Forget. On iPhone, tap the info button next to the network and choose Forget This Network.
5. Turn off or uninstall VPN and security apps, then test again. Apple lists these as a common cause.
6. On Android, make sure the date and time are set automatically (Settings > System > Date & time), and try Safe mode: if Wi-Fi works there, a recently installed app is the problem.
7. If the router has separate 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz networks, try the other one. 5 GHz is faster up close; 2.4 GHz reaches farther.
8. On public Wi-Fi in hotels, airports or cafes, open a browser to bring up the sign-in page.
9. As a last resort, reset network settings. iPhone: Settings > General > Transfer or Reset iPhone > Reset > Reset Network Settings. Pixel: Settings > System > Reset options > Reset Bluetooth & Wi-Fi. This erases all saved Wi-Fi passwords, so have them ready.

When to call for help: if no device in the house can get online after a router restart, contact your internet provider about an outage. If your phone can't join any Wi-Fi network anywhere, or the Wi-Fi switch is grayed out even after a restart, contact the phone maker (Apple or your Android manufacturer) or your carrier, because the Wi-Fi hardware may need service. Also install any pending system update once you are back online.

faq.q: Why does my phone say connected but no internet?
faq.a: The phone reached the router, but the router isn't getting internet. Restart the router and modem, and if other devices also fail, contact your provider.

faq.q: Why won't my iPhone connect to Wi-Fi but other devices will?
faq.a: Forget the network and rejoin it, turn off any VPN or security app, restart the iPhone, and as a last step reset network settings.

faq.q: Why is my Wi-Fi grayed out on my iPhone?
faq.a: Apple says to restart the device. If it stays grayed out on every network, contact Apple.

faq.q: Why does my phone keep disconnecting from Wi-Fi?
faq.a: Common causes are weak signal far from the router, a crowded 2.4 GHz band, or a router that needs a restart or firmware update. Moving closer or switching bands often helps.

faq.q: Will resetting network settings delete anything?
faq.a: It removes saved Wi-Fi networks and passwords and VPN settings (on Pixel, Bluetooth pairings too), but not your photos, apps or messages.
